name: markups-mention
note: Every markup type markups.py knows: a LINK (target is blank unless the href is an in-page #anchor), a USER mention (a medium.com/u/ URL, and it ignores href entirely), STRONG, EM and CODE (whose class uses single quotes in the template). It also covers the two drop paths — an A with an anchorType that is neither LINK nor USER, and a markup type with no template. Deliberately absent: a LINK with no href key. The legacy reads it with markup["href"] rather than .get, so it raises KeyError and kills the whole parse, while the IR defaults it to the empty string; a fixture for it would abort the reference rather than compare anything, and the GraphQL query fetches href as non-null, so the payload cannot produce it.
